Sarah — great context, thanks. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (pricing/ops) so we can put together a couple of viable options before your Nov 21 exec review.

Quick high-level answers while we prepare the proposal:

1) Annualize (12-month commit)
- Pros: typically lowers per-token price by 10–25% depending on commit uplift; simplifies budgeting and avoids monthly variability.
- Cons: requires a committed ARR number and early invoicing (we usually invoice quarterly upfront for annualized commits).

2) Spike protection options
- Burst pocket (reserved burst pool): you pre-purchase a modest burst allowance (e.g., extra 4–6M tokens/month) that drops into a separate bucket. Good for predictable seasonal spikes.
- Soft-throttle with graceband: keeps requests live by applying degraded rate limits at pre-agreed thresholds; cheaper but does not guarantee throughput.
- On-demand overage (pay-as-you-go): auto-consumption beyond commit at a higher per-token rate; easiest operationally but can spike costs.

We can model a blended option: annualize to lower base unit cost + small burst pocket for short spikes + a soft overage cap to prevent runaway bills.

I'll circulate a formal proposal (2–3 options with pricing and billing cadence) by Nov 20. Any preference on invoicing cadence (quarterly vs monthly upfront)?

—Jonas
